role.altitude: She still compiles the record, accepts every code, assigns the group, and prepares the form. She stops hunting a stored record card, a stored classification title, and a stored group row, and she stops retyping fields that are already on the record. She does not gain a right to let a list maintain the record, let a draft stand as the code, let a table assign the group, or let a filled form leave the office.
skills_to_grow: Compile from the paper note when the patient record list is blank
Code from the classification book when the draft does not run
Assign the group from the grouping book when the table row is blank
Prepare the form by hand when a required field is missing
role.ambitious_version: She still maintains the record, accepts the code, assigns the group and prepares the form. A blank note stays blank, a code she has not accepted is not filed, and a form she has not checked does not leave.

tasks.short: Compile and maintain patients' medical records of condition and treatment.

steps.what: List stored medical records for these patients in the patient record.
Read the note of condition and treatment.
Decide which gaps to compile into the record.
Write, in the patient record, the entry she will maintain to document condition and treatment.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} patient record lists the stored card for this patient before she reads the note. She still decides what to compile and she writes the entry she will maintain. The list does not fill the record, does not raise an alert, and does not send data for research, cost control or care improvement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition and treatment sat in a note she had to find across screens and paper before she could maintain the record.
tasks.enabler_now: The patient record can list a stored card when identifier, date, condition and treatment are already fields. Reading the note and writing the entry stay hers.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see whether the note documents the condition and the treatment. A list cannot compile a blank note.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can decide what the record must still document, and only she writes that entry.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the note, decides what to compile, and maintains the entry. She stops hunting the stored card. She does not gain a right to let the list write the record or send it for research.

reach.task: Write the clinical note of condition and treatment.
reach.learn: Which fields the record list can show, and that a blank note stays blank until she compiles it.

evidence.claim: The medical dossier is kept for 20 years, and a patient may ask who viewed it. Sharing patient information by fax is banned. The list shows a stored card inside that dossier. It does not change the retention period and it does not fax the dossier.
Health data are a special category. The list reads the patient record the workplace already keeps. It does not send the note elsewhere.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a data-protection assessment. Whether this workplace's volume meets that duty is not decided here.
The range is a scenario for a card she no longer hunts and a note she still has to read and maintain. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The stored card fields are patient identifier, encounter date, condition text and treatment text. The producer is the treating clinician, who wrote them into the patient record before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.

The lookup key is the patient identifier and encounter date on her work list, produced by the clinic schedule before this task. If either key is missing, or the condition or treatment text is blank, the list step does not run. She compiles from the paper note, and reading, deciding and writing stay at full time. A blank is not filled with a guess.
The maintained entry (condition, treatment, what she added) is produced by her when she writes it. That step stays at full time. The list does not fill that entry.
Reading the note and deciding what to compile stay at full time. The only shortened step is listing a card that is already stored.
The list does not fill the record, does not raise an alert, and does not send data for research, cost control or care improvement. It does not score her.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when a stored field name no longer matches the dossier. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether condition and treatment are stored as fields or only as free text.
Whether this workplace's volume of health records needs a data-protection assessment.
How often the stored card disagrees with the paper note.
research_questions: On a week of records, how often are condition and treatment already stored as fields before she opens the record?
How often does the stored card disagree with the paper note?

incremental.description: Tell the office when a stored field name no longer matches the dossier. The list does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When identifier, date, condition and treatment are already stored, she skips hunting the card. When the list is blank, she compiles from the paper note and the saving is zero. Reading the note, deciding what to compile, and writing the entry are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify, compile, abstract and code with a standard classification.

steps.what: Read the patient note in the patient record before any proposal.
Identify, compile and abstract the facts the note supports.
Draft one code from the patient record using the standard classification file.

loop.input: The sentence she marked in the note, plus code, title and inclusion text from the classification file.
loop.output: One proposed code and the sentence it rests on.
loop.check: She reads whether the proposed code names the same condition the note states, not whether the code number equals a stored field.
loop.stop: One proposal. If she marked no sentence, or the classification file has no title for it, the draft stops and proposes nothing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed lookup cannot read the wording of a clinical note.

steps.what: Accept or rewrite that code in the patient record.

tasks.design: She marks the sentence in the {OTHER} patient record, and a bounded draft proposes one code from the {DOCS} classification file. She reads whether that code means the same condition, and she writes the accepted code. The draft does not write the code, does not raise an alert, does not send a claim, and does not fill a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: She had to search a classification book from free text, and a lookup could not read the note.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can propose one code from a sentence she has already marked and from a classification file the office already keeps. She still accepts or rewrites the code.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to judge whether the proposed code means the condition the note states.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can accept the code. A draft she has not accepted is not the dossier code.
tasks.altitude: She still identifies the facts and accepts every code. The draft only proposes one code from a sentence she marked. She does not gain a right to let a code pass unreviewed.

reach.task: Maintain the classification file of code, title and inclusion text.
reach.learn: The draft uses only that file. A blank file means she codes from the book.

evidence.claim: Dutch Hospital Data codes day admissions to ICD-10 from clinical text.

The same account says codes it treats as high certainty can skip the coder, and coders review the rest. Those are provider figures. This task does not skip her, and the time range does not use those figures.
Software with a medical purpose is a medical device. This draft only proposes a code for her to accept. That regulation does not settle whether this proposal is a device.
Health data are a special category. The draft reads a sentence already in the patient record. It does not send the note elsewhere.
Logging coder corrections can count as staff monitoring that needs works-council consent. This task records the accepted code on the patient record. It does not keep a correction score.
The range is a scenario for a proposal she still has to read against the note. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The sentence that states the condition is already in the patient record. The producer is the treating clinician. She marks that sentence in this task before the draft runs. If she has not marked a sentence, the draft does not run.

The classification file fields are code, title and inclusion text. The producer is the health information technologist, before this task. That upkeep is not counted as time saved here. If the file is blank, the draft does not run and she codes from the book. That coding time stays in the accept step at full time.
The draft reads the marked sentence inside the patient record. It does not send the note to an external model. If the workplace cannot keep that read inside the record, the draft does not run.

The draft outputs one proposed code and the sentence it rests on. It does not write the code, does not raise an alert, does not send a claim, and does not fill a sheet. It is not gated because it does not take effect. She writes the accepted code herself.

The check is whether the code means the same condition the note states. She produces the accepted code by writing it. That step stays at full time. A correction is the dossier code, not a staff score. This design does not copy a rule that skips the coder.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the health information office when a classification title is wrong. That telling is her own speech. The draft does not send it.
unknowns: Whether this workplace can run the draft inside the patient record without sending the note out.
Whether this code draft is software with a medical purpose.
Whether the classification file covers this specialty.
research_questions: On a week of notes, how often has she marked a sentence that already has a title in the classification file?
How often does she rewrite the proposed code after reading the note?

incremental.description: Tell the health information office when a classification title is wrong. The draft does not send that correction, and it is not logged as a score.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When she has marked a sentence and the classification file has a title, the draft replaces the search for one code. When the sentence or the file is blank, she codes from the book and the saving is zero. Identifying the facts and accepting the code are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign the patient to a diagnosis-related group in software.

steps.what: Read the accepted diagnosis code for this patient.
List one stored match from the diagnosis-related groups table in the patient record.
Decide whether to assign that group to this patient.
Record the group in the appropriate computer software.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} patient record lists one stored row from the grouping table for the code she already accepted. She still decides whether to assign that group, and she records it. The list does not assign the group, does not raise an alert, does not send it, and does not fill a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: She had to look up the group for an accepted code in software that did not show the one stored row.
tasks.enabler_now: A grouping table the office already keeps can list the one stored row for an accepted code. Deciding and recording the group stay hers.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to decide whether that row is the right group for this admission. A table cannot assign it.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can assign the group. A stored row she has not accepted is not the recorded group.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the accepted code, decides the group, and records it. She stops hunting the table row. She does not gain a right to let the list assign or send the group.

reach.task: Maintain the grouping table from an accepted code to a group label.
reach.learn: The list shows one stored row. It does not assign the group, and a blank row means she uses the grouping book.

evidence.claim: A stored code can be matched to one stored group label by the table the workplace already files. That match is a lookup. It is not a measured saving. Model knowledge.
Health data are a special category. The list reads the accepted code and the group row inside the patient record. It does not send the group elsewhere.
The medical dossier is kept for 20 years. Sharing patient information by fax is banned. The recorded group stays in the dossier. The list does not fax it.
The range is a scenario for a table row she no longer hunts and a group she still has to assign. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The accepted code fields are code and title, already on the patient record. The producer is her own earlier coding, or a colleague coder, before this task. That coding is not counted as time saved here. If the code is missing, the list does not run and she assigns from the grouping book. Deciding and recording stay at full time.

The grouping table fields are code and group label. The producer is the health information technologist, before this task. The table is the grouping set this workplace already files. This task does not name that set and does not transmit a group.
She reads the accepted code before the list uses it. The list shows one stored row. It does not assign the group, does not raise an alert, does not send the group, and does not fill a sheet.
Deciding whether to assign the group, and recording the group in the patient record, stay at full time. The only shortened step is listing a row that is already stored.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when the table maps a code to the wrong label. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Which grouping set this workplace already files.
How often one accepted code maps to more than one group row.
Whether this workplace transmits groups at all, which this task does not do.
research_questions: On a week of admissions, how often does the accepted code already have one group row before she looks?
How often does she refuse the stored row after reading the admission?

incremental.description: Tell the office when the grouping table maps a code to the wrong label. The list does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the accepted code is on the record and the table has one row, she skips hunting that row. When the code or the row is blank, she assigns from the grouping book and the saving is zero. Deciding the group and recording it are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Process and prepare business or government forms.

steps.what: Read the fields the business or government form needs.
Fill one of the prepared forms from patient record fields only.
Check that the filled forms still mean those fields.
Prepare the correction when that check fails.
Process the handoff of the accepted form herself.

tasks.design: After she confirms the fields, a fill step writes filled form v1 from the {DOCS} template and the {OTHER} patient record. She must accept that exact version before it stands; she prepares any correction herself and she processes the handoff. The fill does not send the form, does not raise an alert, and does not file it.
tasks.previous_blocker: She retyped fields that were already on the patient record onto each form, then still had to check the meaning.
tasks.enabler_now: A template can copy confirmed fields into filled form v1. She still checks that version, prepares any correction, and hands the form over.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see whether the filled form means the same facts she confirmed. A copy cannot judge that.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can accept the filled form. A version she has not accepted does not leave.
tasks.altitude: She still confirms the fields, accepts or corrects the form, and hands it over. She stops retyping fields that are already stored. She does not gain a right to let the fill send or file the form.

reach.task: Keep the form template and the names of the boxes it copies.
reach.learn: The fill copies only fields she has confirmed. It does not send the form, and a missing field means she prepares it by hand.

evidence.claim: Sharing patient information by fax is banned, and the dossier is kept for 20 years. The fill copies fields onto a form inside the workplace. It does not fax the form and it does not file it.
Health data are a special category. The fill copies fields already in the patient record onto the workplace form. It does not send those fields elsewhere.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a data-protection assessment. Whether these forms meet that duty is not decided here.
The range is a scenario for fields she no longer retypes and a form she still has to check and hand over. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The confirmed fields are patient identifier, encounter date, accepted code and group label. The producer is the maintained patient record from earlier work. She reads them in this task before the fill. If any required field is blank, the fill does not run and she prepares the form by hand. Checking, correcting and handing over stay at full time.
The form template fields are the template name and the blank boxes those four fields map to. The producer is the records office, before this task. That upkeep is not counted as time saved here.

The fill writes filled form v1 and nothing else. She accepts that exact version in the check step. A change voids that acceptance, and she prepares the form herself. The fill does not take effect without that acceptance.

The fill does not send the form, does not fax it, does not raise an alert, and does not file it with a business partner or with government. She processes the handoff herself. That step stays at full time.
Checking the meaning and preparing a correction stay at full time. The only shortened step is copying fields that are already stored.
Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the records office when a template box names the wrong field. That telling is her own speech. The fill does not send it.
unknowns: Which of these forms are business forms and which are government forms.
Whether this workplace's volume of forms needs a data-protection assessment.
How often a confirmed field is present but means something the template box does not.
research_questions: On a week of forms, how often are all four fields already stored before she prepares the form?
How often does she reject filled form v1 after reading it against the note?

incremental.description: Tell the records office when a template box names the wrong field. The fill does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the four fields are already stored, the fill replaces retyping them onto filled form v1, and she still accepts that exact version. When a field is blank, or she changes the form, she prepares it herself and the saving is zero. Checking, correcting, and handing the form over are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
